subject.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core ship and maintain a standalone Rust launcher in addition to the existing CLI and platform application surfaces?
rationale: The PR adds a new executable, toolchain, packaging target, and long-term compatibility obligation rather than repairing an established behavior contract, so product ownership cannot be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Use existing launch surfaces
options.body: Do not add the generic core launcher; improve the existing CLI, setup flow, dashboard, or platform application entry points instead.

options.title: Sponsor the core launcher
options.body: Assign an owner and require a focused branch, native cross-platform discovery, compatibility coverage, packaging integration, and current-head Windows and Unix proof.

options.title: Maintain an external companion
options.body: Publish the thin wrapper as a separately maintained companion project that invokes OpenClaw's public CLI without joining the core release surface.

recommendation.title: Use existing launch surfaces
recommendation.body: Do not add the generic core launcher; improve the existing CLI, setup flow, dashboard, or platform application entry points instead.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a repository product-boundary and executable-ownership decision rather than a narrow implementation choice.
